steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Functionalist view: education serves vital functions for society. Durkheim: education transmits society's norms and values (social solidarity) and teaches specialist skills for the division of labour. Parsons: education is the main agent of secondary socialisation and a bridge between family and wider society; it promotes meritocracy (everyone has equal opportunity to succeed based on ability and effort).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marxist view: education serves capitalism. Althusser: education is an Ideological State Apparatus (ISA) that transmits ruling class ideology, making inequality seem natural and inevitable. Bowles and Gintis: the correspondence principle - schools mirror the workplace through the hidden curriculum (hierarchy, competition, obedience to authority, punctuality) preparing workers for capitalist exploitation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Feminist view: education is patriarchal. Historically: girls were steered towards domestic subjects and away from science/maths. Kelly: the curriculum is male-dominated (textbooks feature men, examples from male experiences). Modern challenge: despite girls outperforming boys, women still face a glass ceiling in careers and are underrepresented in STEM subjects.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The hidden curriculum: the unwritten, unofficial lessons that schools teach - obedience to authority, competition, conformity, acceptance of hierarchy, punctuality. Functionalists see this as positive (teaches social norms); Marxists see it as negative (prepares workers for exploitation).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare Functionalist and Marxist views of the role of education. | Explain what the hidden curriculum is and evaluate its importance in education. | Evaluate whether the education system is meritocratic.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Functionalism: education = SOCIAL SOLIDARITY + MERITOCRACY. Marxism: education = IDEOLOGICAL CONTROL + CORRESPONDENCE PRINCIPLE. Hidden curriculum: obedience + hierarchy + competition + punctuality. Functionalists say POSITIVE. Marxists say NEGATIVE. Meritocracy: claimed but NOT fully achieved - class, gender and ethnicity affect outcomes.
